title: three-horizon-planning-slate-and-allhands-orchestrator-v0-1
body:
Purpose:
This is a working slate for the company-wide three-horizon planning exercise and the companion all-hands orchestration notes. Goal: produce a concise Q2 priority map, a single-page company OKR draft, and a run-of-show + comms checklist for the all-hands.

TL;DR (for execs):
- Narrow to 3 company priorities this quarter (one per horizon cluster) to reduce org dispersion.
- Validate cost/latency playbook for Redwood Dedicated to reduce unit cost 10% by end of quarter.
- Launch initial Private VPC reference for 2 pilot customers with tightened SLOs and KMS integration.
- All-hands will present: strategy framing (10m), 3 priority owners (5m each), product demos (20m), Q&A + commit asks (15m).

Quick context / notes to self:
- Workshop with GTM and Eng next Wed (2025-02-19) to align customer milestones and go/no-go for Private pilot.
- Finance wants a crisp forecast: incremental ARR from Dedicated contracts and expected IRR on Reserved capacity buys. Ask FP&A for model by 2025-02-21.
- Risk: If model onboarding takes >6 weeks for pilot customers, push Private pilot start and surface to execs immediately.

Three-horizon priority map (working definitions):
- Horizon 1 (Core reliability + economics): deliverables that keep the platform healthy and cost-competitive. Owners: SRE + Serving Runtime.
  - Focus examples: 99.95% cluster uptime for Dedicated pools, token unit cost down-target -10% via batching + kernel sweeps.
- Horizon 2 (Productization + scale): features that help customers adopt Redwood and increase ARR. Owners: Product Hosted API + Console.
  - Focus examples: per-route token-level cost visibility shipped to Console, rollout automation for model pinning.
- Horizon 3 (Expansion / strategic bets): longer-term efforts that open new markets. Owners: Private Deployments + Solutions Eng.
  - Focus examples: VPC/on-prem quickstart with KMS/HSM integration, marketplace partner feed, regulated vertical tooling.

Draft Company-level OKRs (company-wide, single-page draft):
- Objective A: Deliver predictable, low-cost inference for production teams.
  - KR1: Reduce average per-token cost (hosted + dedicated blended) by 10% vs baseline (Q1).
  - KR2: Achieve median p99 latency for common 2k-length prompts < 400ms on Dedicated SKU under 80% load.
  - KR3: Increase active paying projects using per-route analytics to 40 (from 18).

- Objective B: Expand and operationalize Private deployments for regulated customers.
  - KR1: Onboard 2 pilot customers into Private VPC with full audit logs and KMS by end of quarter.
  - KR2: Harden the Private control plane for 99.9% availability in customer test windows.
  - KR3: Produce a certified compliance checklist for SOC2-like controls for Private by end of quarter.

- Objective C: Improve developer adoption and retention across PLG funnel.
  - KR1: Increase API-to-paid conversion within 30 days by 25%.
  - KR2: Reduce time-to-first-response (sample app) from 20 min -> 8 min via new quickstarts and templates.
  - KR3: Ship 3 reference workloads (search, summarization, agent template) with verifiable perf profiles.

Notes on measurability and owner alignment:
- Each KR needs a single primary owner (team lead) and a secondary owner in Eng/Platform. Add owners column for final draft.
- Metrics owners: Product Analytics will be the source of truth for conversion + usage metrics; SRE will provide latency and availability measurements.
- Need to document baseline values before finalizing KRs (ask analytics for Q1 baselines by Feb 18).

All-hands run-of-show (45 min total, flexible):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome + candids (CEO) — big-picture framing and one line on macro strategy.
- 0:05–0:15 — Strategy deep-dive (Head of Product) — three-horizon map, why we picked the priorities.
- 0:15–0:30 — Priority owner lightning demos (3x 5 min):
    - H1 owner (SRE lead): reliability and cost wins — show before/after perf graphs.
    - H2 owner (Product lead): demo per-route analytics console + rollout flow.
    - H3 owner (Solutions Eng): show Private quickstart and customer playbook.
- 0:30–0:40 — Customer spotlight (Pre-recorded demo + short live Q&A) — show one pilot or reference customer story.
- 0:40–0:47 — Exec asks & commitments (People Ops + Finance) — hires, budget asks, and runway signals.
- 0:47–0:55 — Live Q&A (moderated via Slido) + close.

All-hands logistics and checklist (owner in parentheses):
- Slide deck draft to exec review (CEO + Head of Product) by 2025-02-18 (Riley Chen).
- Rehearsal run for priority owners on 2025-02-20 10am PT (Aisha Kapoor to coordinate).
- Recorded customer snippet capture (Marisol Vega) — ask Solutions Eng to produce 2-minute clip.
- Internal comms: pre-announce + brief to managers 48h pre (People Ops).
- Post-all-hands follow-up doc with concrete team asks and playbook links (Product Ops).

Exec update bullets (one-pagers to include):
- Status vs last quarter: quick 3-line progress for each priority.
- Key risks and mitigations (financial runway, pilot delays, infra debt).
- Decisions needed this week: e.g., approve $300k for reserved capacity for Dedicated pilot; green light for two Private pilot customers.
- Ask ledger: headcount (engineer hires), tooling budget (observability retention), marketplace partner investment.

Communications plan (comm channels + cadence):
- Pre-announce all-hands via email + slack channel (#company-allhands) two days prior.
- Share one-pager OKR draft in Confluence with comment window open for 48 hours post-all-hands.
- Priority owner office hours: schedule 2x 45m sessions post-all-hands for deep dives.

Decision points for leadership (to surface in the exec sync):
- Approve top-line KRs and metrics owners by 2025-02-21.
- Approve Dedicated capacity reservation spend (ask amount + commit term) by 2025-02-24.
- Approve Private pilot customer list and NDA flow by 2025-02-25.

Open questions / things to research before finalizing:
- Can we get a reliable per-token cost delta estimate for the new KV-cache optimizations? (ask Serving Runtime team).
- What is the minimal SLO bundle for Private that keeps compliance teams comfortable but doesn’t blow engineering staffing?
- Are there legal/regulatory constraints for two target pilot customers (Europe APAC constraints for data residency)?

Next steps and owners (first pass):
- Product Ops: assemble final one-page OKR doc (Riley Chen) — due 2025-02-21.
- Serving Runtime: cost/latency runbook + ETA for kernel-level improvements (Samir Gupta) — due 2025-02-19.
- Solutions Eng: Private pilot checklist + customer comms draft (Marisol Vega) — due 2025-02-22.
- Finance/FP&A: model for Dedicated capacity ROI and ARR impact (Jonah Park) — due 2025-02-21.

Notes to owners (informal):
- Keep language simple for execs — one metric + one sentence per KR.
- Make the all-hands slides actionable — include clear team asks (who does what in 2 weeks).
- If a KR is not measurable in the first pass, mark as 'needs instrumentation' and add metric owner.

Appendix (scratch):
- Suggested templated phrasing for all-hands slide: "Our focus this quarter is to make Redwood the most reliable, cost-efficient inference platform for production teams. We will measure success by X, Y, Z. Here are the owner-level commitments."
- Quick rehearsal script for CEO (bullet): open with one anecdote about a customer disruption solved by fallbacks, then tie to the importance of operational reliability.

-- end of draft --

(Work-in-progress: this doc will be iterated after the cross-functional priority workshop and the exec sync; keep comments inline in Confluence and use this Drive doc for the rehearsal notes)
